name: Whole corrected sentence with Python-derived spans v1
scope: Development only. Compare one candidate run to the finalized archived Qwen4B baseline, not a contemporaneous randomized speed trial. No app changes or held-out inference.
change: Request corrected_text plus one explanation; derive at most two token edit regions using exact Python offsets. Same example sentences, model and decoding settings; explanation instructions retain the actual-rule requirement. The schema changes how explanations are represented (one per response).
mechanical_rejection: Wrong keys/types/bounds, changed text without explanation, unchanged text with nonempty explanation, more than two derived regions, or failure to reconstruct. Retain raw output; rejection is not a no-error success.
selection_requirements: All 30 acceptable inputs remain unchanged without rejection or service failure.
More than 17/30 useful explained corrections under the approved rubric and no decrease below baseline accepted-edit precision (80%).
Rejection count must not exceed baseline 4/60; no mean/median-only latency claims.
Before adoption, select on development, then review/freeze fresh held-out labels and meet the existing two-run held-out gates.
diagnostics: Exact-reference sentence matches and reconstruction are mechanical diagnostics, not semantic success. Review all changed/rejected sentences and explanations. Repeat a promising candidate before attributing improvement to the design.
learning_limitations: Token diff may produce more than one region for one linguistic edit; human review must resolve alignment rather than forcing one-to-one edit counts. Output schema alone cannot establish correctness, meaning preservation or pronunciation.
